title: Integrated CTO capstone
objectives: Synthesise delivery, tech, economics, product and people decisions into one CTO narrative
Defend a multi-quarter technology strategy with evidence and trade-offs
Produce an integrated decision record and review plan
Communicate the strategy to board and executive stakeholders
verificationNotes: The capstone is Original Academy material and is not tied to a single official page.
All figures and decisions must be labelled REAL, ASSUMPTION or SIMULATED.

sections.heading: What a capstone integrates
sections.body: A CTO capstone combines the threads from every pillar: delivery metrics and risk, architecture and security, cost and investment, product strategy and metrics, people and organisation. The point is not to repeat lessons but to make trade-offs across them. A decision that improves cost may slow delivery; a people change may enable architecture; a product bet changes the risk profile.

sections.heading: Building the narrative
sections.body: Start with the business outcome and the constraint. Then show the current state with evidence, the options considered, the decision and its cost, the risks and mitigations, the people and delivery plan, and the measures that would change the decision. Keep one page for executives and a deeper record for reviewers.

sections.heading: Defending across pillars
sections.body: A credible defence handles cross-pillar questions: why this architecture for this product, at this cost, with this team, on this timeline, with these risks. Weak answers optimise one pillar and ignore the others. Strong answers name the trade-off and the evidence.

workedExample.title: Capstone outline for Cretek (illustrative)
workedExample.body: Outcome: reduce incident recovery time and cost per school while launching a new analytics product. Constraints: data residency, two engineers available, 200,000 budget. Decisions: consolidate on one cloud, introduce an event-driven reporting pipeline, hire one platform engineer, defer a second product. Risks: migration slippage, skill gaps. Measures: RTO, cost per school, delivery lead time, NPS.

misconceptions: Treating the capstone as a single-pillar exercise.
Presenting a plan with no trade-offs.
Using slides without a decision record.
learn.explainTask: In 200 words or fewer, explain your integrated CTO strategy for the next two quarters to a board.

build.business: Cretek needs an integrated technology strategy across delivery, architecture, cost, product and people.
build.problem: Produce an integrated CTO capstone: a two-quarter strategy with decision records, cost and risk models, delivery plan and communication artefacts.
requirements: State the business outcome and constraints
Integrate at least three pillars in the decision
Produce decision records with alternatives and reversal triggers
Model cost and risk with labelled assumptions
Produce a one-page executive summary and a deeper record
Every figure labelled REAL, ASSUMPTION or SIMULATED
constraints: Must be reproducible from the repository
build.design: Write a one-page strategy and a supporting decision log.
build.deliverable: Integrated capstone strategy, decision log, cost and risk model, and executive summary, referenced by path.

defend.scenario: The board asks for a single, credible technology strategy for the next two quarters.
prompts: What outcome are you targeting and how will you measure it?
Which trade-offs did you make across cost, delivery and people?
What would make you reverse the decision?
What are the top three risks and who owns them?
How does this fit the company strategy?

rubric.criterion: Risks and reversal triggers are credible
